theorem logCounting_zero_ge_of_lattice_zeros {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g Set.univ) (hgo : ∀ z, meromorphicOrderAt g z ≠ ⊤)
    {T : ℂ} (hT : T ≠ 0) (hzero : ∀ n : ℤ, g ((n : ℂ) * T) = 0)
    {r : ℝ} (hr1 : 1 ≤ r) :
    Real.log 2 * (r / ‖T‖ - 2) ≤ ValueDistribution.logCounting g 0 r
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem logCounting_zero_ge_of_lattice_zeros {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g Set.univ) (hgo : ∀ z, meromorphicOrderAt g z ≠ ⊤)
    {T : ℂ} (hT : T ≠ 0) (hzero : ∀ n : ℤ, g ((n : ℂ) * T) = 0)
    {r : ℝ} (hr1 : 1 ≤ r) :
    Real.log 2 * (r / ‖T‖ - 2) ≤ ValueDistribution.logCounting g 0 r
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  classical
  have hTpos : (0 : ℝ) < ‖T‖ := norm_pos_iff.mpr hT
  set N : ℕ := ⌊r / (2 * ‖T‖)⌋₊ with hN
  set F : Finset ℤ := latticeIndices r T with hF
  have hNle : (N : ℝ) ≤ r / (2 * ‖T‖) := Nat.floor_le (by positivity)
  have hNge : r / (2 * ‖T‖) - 1 ≤ (N : ℝ) := le_of_lt (Nat.sub_one_lt_floor _)
  -- every index is small
  have hindex : ∀ n ∈ F, ‖((n : ℂ) * T)‖ ≤ r / 2 ∧ (n : ℂ) * T ≠ 0 := by
    intro n hn
    have hn0 : n ≠ 0 := Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hn
    have hnIcc : n ∈ Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) (N : ℤ) := Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hn
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at hnIcc
    have habs : |(n : ℝ)| ≤ (N : ℝ) := by
      rw [abs_le]
      constructor
      · exact_mod_cast hnIcc.1
      · exact_mod_cast hnIcc.2
    constructor
    · rw [norm_mul, norm_intCast]
      calc |(n : ℝ)| * ‖T‖ ≤ (N : ℝ) * ‖T‖ := by nlinarith [hTpos]
        _ ≤ (r / (2 * ‖T‖)) * ‖T‖ := by nlinarith [hTpos]
        _ = r / 2 := by field_simp
    · intro hcon
      rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hcon with h | h
      · exact hn0 (by exact_mod_cast h)
      · exact hT h
  -- the divisor supported on the lattice points
  set D₀ : Function.locallyFinsupp ℂ ℤ :=
    ∑ n ∈ F, Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single ((n : ℂ) * T) 1 with hD₀
  have hinj : ∀ m n : ℤ, (m : ℂ) * T = (n : ℂ) * T → m = n := by
    intro m n hmn
    have := mul_right_cancel₀ hT hmn
    exact_mod_cast this
  -- each lattice point carries a zero of `g`
  have horder : ∀ n : ℤ, 1 ≤ divisor g Set.univ ((n : ℂ) * T) := by
    intro n
    set z : ℂ := (n : ℂ) * T with hz
    have hmem : z ∈ (Set.univ : Set ℂ) := Set.mem_univ z
    have hmero : MeromorphicOn g Set.univ := fun x _ => (hg x (Set.mem_univ x)).meromorphicAt
    rw [MeromorphicOn.divisor_apply hmero hmem]
    have hne : meromorphicOrderAt g z ≠ ⊤ := hgo z
    have hanal : AnalyticAt ℂ g z := hg z hmem
    have hz' : z = (n : ℂ) * T := hz
    have hmap : meromorphicOrderAt g z = ENat.map Nat.cast (analyticOrderAt g z) :=
      hanal.meromorphicOrderAt_eq
    have hazero : analyticOrderAt g z ≠ 0 := by
      intro hcon
      rcases analyticOrderAt_eq_zero.mp hcon with h | h
      · exact h hanal
      · exact h (by simpa [hz] using hzero n)
    have hatop : analyticOrderAt g z ≠ ⊤ := by
      intro hcon
      apply hne
      rw [hmap, hcon]
      rfl
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ : ∃ k : ℕ, analyticOrderAt g z = (k : ℕ∞) := by
      cases h : analyticOrderAt g z with
      | top => exact absurd h hatop
      | coe k => exact ⟨k, rfl⟩
    have hk1 : 1 ≤ k := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with h | h
      · rw [h] at hk
        exact absurd (by simpa using hk) hazero
      · exact h
    rw [hmap, hk]
    simp only [ENat.map_coe]
    rw [WithTop.untop₀_coe]
    exact_mod_cast hk1
  have hD₀le : D₀ ≤ (divisor g Set.univ)⁺ := by
    intro z
    have hsum : D₀ z = ∑ n ∈ F, (if z = (n : ℂ) * T then (1 : ℤ) else 0) := by
      rw [hD₀]
      simp only [Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.coe_sum, Finset.sum_apply,
        Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single_apply]
    rw [hsum]
    by_cases hex : ∃ n ∈ F, z = (n : ℂ) * T
    · obtain ⟨n, hnF, rfl⟩ := hex
      have hone : ∑ m ∈ F, (if (n : ℂ) * T = (m : ℂ) * T then (1 : ℤ) else 0) = 1 := by
        rw [Finset.sum_eq_single n]
        · simp
        · intro m _ hmn
          rw [if_neg]
          intro hcon
          exact hmn (hinj n m hcon).symm
        · intro hcon
          exact absurd hnF hcon
      rw [hone]
      have := horder n
      have hpos : (divisor g Set.univ)⁺ ((n : ℂ) * T)
          = max (divisor g Set.univ ((n : ℂ) * T)) 0 := rfl
      rw [hpos]
      exact le_max_of_le_left this
    · push_neg at hex
      have hzero' : ∑ n ∈ F, (if z = (n : ℂ) * T then (1 : ℤ) else 0) = 0 := by
        refine Finset.sum_eq_zero ?_
        intro n hn
        rw [if_neg (hex n hn)]
      rw [hzero']
      exact posPart_nonneg _
  -- the counting function of the lattice divisor
  have hcount : Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting D₀ r
      = ∑ n ∈ F, (Real.log r - Real.log ‖((n : ℂ) * T)‖) := by
    rw [hD₀, map_sum, Finset.sum_apply]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    intro n hn
    have hle : ‖((n : ℂ) * T)‖ ≤ r := le_trans (hindex n hn).1 (by linarith)
    rw [Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting_single_eq_log_sub_const hle]
    simp
  have hterm : ∀ n ∈ F, Real.log 2 ≤ Real.log r - Real.log ‖((n : ℂ) * T)‖ := by
    intro n hn
    obtain ⟨hle, hne⟩ := hindex n hn
    have hpos : 0 < ‖((n : ℂ) * T)‖ := norm_pos_iff.mpr hne
    rw [← Real.log_div (by linarith) (ne_of_gt hpos)]
    refine Real.log_le_log (by norm_num) ?_
    rw [le_div_iff₀ hpos]
    linarith
  have hlow : Real.log 2 * (2 * (N : ℝ))
      ≤ Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting D₀ r := by
    rw [hcount]
    calc Real.log 2 * (2 * (N : ℝ)) = ∑ _n ∈ F, Real.log 2 := by
          rw [Finset.sum_const, hF, card_latticeIndices, ← hN, nsmul_eq_mul]
          push_cast
          ring
      _ ≤ ∑ n ∈ F, (Real.log r - Real.log ‖((n : ℂ) * T)‖) := Finset.sum_le_sum hterm
  -- compare with the counting funct

by
  let g : ℂ → ℂ := fun z => F z - a
  have hgdiff : Differentiable ℂ g := by
    dsimp only [g]
    fun_prop
  have hC' : 1 ≤ C + ‖a‖ := by linarith [norm_nonneg a]
  have hggrow : ∀ z : ℂ, ‖g z‖ ≤ (C + ‖a‖) * Real.exp (A * ‖z‖) := by
    intro z
    have hexp : 1 ≤ Real.exp (A * ‖z‖) := by
      rw [Real.one_le_exp_iff]
      positivity
    have haexp : ‖a‖ ≤ ‖a‖ * Real.exp (A * ‖z‖) := by
      simpa only [mul_one] using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hexp (norm_nonneg a)
    calc
      ‖g z‖ = ‖F z - a‖ := rfl
      _ ≤ ‖F z‖ + ‖a‖ := norm_sub_le _ _
      _ ≤ C * Real.exp (A * ‖z‖) + ‖a‖ * Real.exp (A * ‖z‖) :=
        add_le_add (hgrow z) haexp
      _ = (C + ‖a‖) * Real.exp (A * ‖z‖) := by ring
  by_contra hFconst
  have hgne : g ≠ 0 := by
    intro hg
    apply hFconst
    funext z
    have hz := congrFun hg z
    dsimp only [g] at hz
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp hz
  have hgc : ∃ c : ℂ, g c ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra hc
    push Not at hc
    exact hgne (funext hc)
  obtain ⟨c, hgc⟩ := hgc
  obtain ⟨K, hK, hcount⟩ :=
    exponentialType_zeroCount_linear hgdiff hgc hA hC' hggrow
  let δ : ℝ := 1 / (12 * (K + 1))
  have hδ : 0 < δ := by
    dsimp only [δ]
    positivity
  obtain ⟨T₀, hT₀, hwindow⟩ := exists_uniform_riemannZeta_zero_window hδ
  let base : ℝ := 1 + ‖c‖ + T₀ + δ + 2
  have hbase : 0 < base := by
    dsimp only [base]
    have hT₀pos : 0 < T₀ := by linarith
    positivity
  obtain ⟨N : ℕ, hN⟩ := exists_nat_gt (2 * K * base)
  have hNposReal : 0 < (N : ℝ) := by
    have : 0 < 2 * K * base := by positivity

  have hNpos : 0 < N := by exact_mod_cast hNposReal
  obtain ⟨z, hzinj, hxizero, hzbound⟩ :=
    exists_suzukiCentered_zero_packet hδ hT₀ hwindow N
  let r : ℝ := ‖c‖ + T₀ + 3 * δ * N + δ + 2
  have hr : 1 ≤ r := by
    dsimp only [r]
    have hT₀pos : 0 < T₀ := by linarith
    have hterm : 0 ≤ 3 * δ * (N : ℝ) := by positivity
    linarith [norm_nonneg c]
  have hball : ∀ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin N)), z i ∈ closedBall c r := by
    intro i _
    rw [mem_closedBall_iff_norm]
    calc
      ‖z i - c‖ ≤ ‖z i‖ + ‖c‖ := norm_sub_le _ _

        simpa [add_comm] using add_le_add_right (hzbound i) ‖c‖

    intro i _
    dsimp only [g]

    (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin N)) z

    rw [show 3 * K * (1 / (12 * (K + 1))) =

## 7. The residual question, worked and answered negatively

§5 asked: is there a Rankin–Selberg-type construction whose pole order counts off-critical-line
zeros? Working it rather than leaving it open:

**The count exists, and it is classical.** `N(sigma, T)` — the number of zeros with real part
`> sigma` up to height `T` — is a nonnegative integer, produced by counting, with no positive input.
It is a creator in the sense of §1, and RH is exactly `N(sigma, T) = 0` for every `sigma > 1/2`. So
the creator that would settle RH is not missing; it is the zero-density function, and bounding it
(`N(sigma,T) ≪ T^{c(1-sigma)} log T` and its descendants) is a century-old field that has never
reached zero.

**Rankin–Selberg does not reach it.** `n_F = ord_(s=1) R_(F,F)` is the divergence rate of
`sum_p |a_F(p)|^2 / p` — a second moment of the Satake data, averaged over primes, evaluated at one
point on the boundary of absolute convergence. It is a *factorization multiplicity*: it counts how
many primitive factors `F` has, weighted by their exponents. Zero **location** is not a function of
that datum, and the corpus's own `linear-kills-quadratic-survives` is the record of how thin the
invariants in this family are.

So the answer is: **no, as far as I can see.** The Rankin–Selberg creator counts the wrong object,
and the creator that counts the right object — `N(sigma,T)` — is not the pole order of any
constructible thing; it is extracted by contour integration of `zeta'/zeta`, which needs the zeros
one is trying to constrain.

- **ID:** `BEURLING-REGULAR-INTEGERS-NO-CONSTRAINT-001`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper + Lean) / FIREWALL, and a retraction
- **Parent:** `rh-sensitivity-threshold-of-the-prime-measure.md` §6 (whose universal design rule is withdrawn)
- **RH used:** no · **Computation used:** no
- **Scientific status:** density positivity, rational transform and zero are Lean certified;
  the counting estimate in §2(b) is paper-only. Classical continuous Beurling construction;
  no novelty or RH proof claimed.

## One sentence

For each `β ∈ (1/2,1)`, `γ != 0` and selected `θ > 0`, there is a continuous positive-density
model with a genuine zeta zero at `β+iγ`; its paper counting estimate is `N(x)=ρx+O(x^θ)`.
The model depends on `θ`. This refutes sufficiency of that counting estimate in this continuous
class, not its necessity or usefulness in a proof with additional arithmetic hypotheses.
Ordinary integer counting is unconditionally `floor x=x+O(1)`; RH does not assert a bound for it.

## 1. The construction

Work in the logarithmic coordinate `t = log u`.  A positive density `w` on `(0,∞)` with
`∫_0^1 w < ∞` and `w(t) = O(e^{t}/t)` defines a Beurling prime measure `dΠ(u) = w(log u) du/u`
whose zeta is `ζ(s) = exp F(s)`, `F(s) = ∫_0^∞ e^{-st} w(t) dt`, convergent for `Re s > 1`.

Fix `β ∈ (1/2,1)`, `γ ≠ 0`, `δ ∈ (0, 1)`, and a positive integer `A`.  Put

```
w(t) = ( e^{t} + A e^{δ t} − (A − 1) − 2 e^{β t} cos(γ t) ) / t.
```

**Coefficient balance.**  The numerator at `t = 0` is `1 + A − (A−1) − 2 = 0`, so `w` is bounded
near the origin: the system is locally finite.  (This balance is exactly the statement that the
zeta function below has as many zeros as poles counted with multiplicity, hence tends to `1` at
`s = ∞`, as the Laplace transform of a locally finite counting measure with unit mass at the origin must.)

**Positivity.**  Since `cos ≤ 1`,

```
t · w(t) ≥ K(t) := e^{t} + A e^{δ t} − (A − 1) − 2 e^{β t},     K(0) = 0,
K'(t) = e^{t} + A δ e^{δ t} − 2 β e^{β t}.
```

Set `t₀ = log(2β)/(1−β) ≥ 0` (nonnegative because `β > 1/2`).  For `t ≥ t₀` one has
`e^{(1−β)t} ≥ 2β`, hence `e^{t} ≥ 2β e^{β t}` and `K'(t) ≥ 0`.  For `0 ≤ t ≤ t₀` one has
`2β e^{β t} ≤ 2β e^{β t₀} =: C` while `A δ e^{δ t} ≥ A δ`, so `K'(t) ≥ 0` as soon as `A δ ≥ C`,
i.e. as soon as

```
A ≥ ( 2 β e^{β log(2β)/(1−β)} ) / δ.
```

With such an `A`, `K' ≥ 0` on `[0,∞)`, hence `K ≥ K(0) = 0`, hence **`w ≥ 0` on `(0,∞)`**.

**The zeta function.**  Group the numerator as

```
( e^{t} − e^{(β+iγ)t} ) + ( e^{δ t} − e^{(β−iγ)t} ) + (A−1)( e^{δ t} − e^{0·t} ),
```

three Frullani integrands after division by `t`.  Using
`∫_0^∞ (e^{-at} − e^{-bt}) dt/t = Log b − Log a` for `Re a, Re b > 0`, with `Re s > 1`,

```
F(s) = [Log(s−β−iγ) − Log(s−1)] + [Log(s−β+iγ) − Log(s−δ)]
        + (A−1)[Log(s) − Log(s−δ)],
```

so that

```
ζ(s) = exp F(s) = ( (s−β)² + γ² ) · s^{A−1} / ( (s−1) · (s−δ)^A ).
```

## 2. What the system does

**(a) Zeros off the critical line.**  `ζ(β + iγ) = 0`, and the denominator
`(β+iγ−1)(β+iγ−δ)^A` is nonzero because its factors have imaginary part `γ ≠ 0`.  So `β ± iγ` are
genuine zeros, with `β > 1/2` arbitrary in `(1/2, 1)`.  **RH fails for this system, arbitrarily
badly.**

**(b) A counting bound at the selected exponent — paper only.** The rational function has
residue `ρ=((1−β)^2+γ^2)/(1−δ)^A > 0` at `1`. Partial fractions of `ζ(s)/s` give a counting
function of the form

```

```

Here a constant term can occur from the origin. For each `θ>δ`, the polynomial factor is
`O(x^(θ−δ))`, giving `N(x)=ρx+O(x^θ)`. Choosing `δ<θ` constructs a suitable model for each
requested exponent. The pole at the positive number `δ` prevents this argument from yielding all

**(c) Prime and integer measures are distinct.** The continuous logarithmic-prime counting

proved by the Lean theorem. In particular, a discretization theorem cannot be inferred from the
rational transform alone.

# Transverse divisor relocation preserving the ordinate counting measure requires even multiplicity

- **ID:** `relocation-blindness-requires-even-multiplicity`
- **Stage:** 1-in-progress
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper, elementary) + SCOPE CORRECTION
- **Scientific status:** `[PAPER-PROVED]` `[SCOPE CORRECTION TO AN EXISTING NO-GO]` `[NOT AN RH PROOF]`
- **Corrects the scope of:**
  `2-fully-proven/not_new_scientific_knowledge/11-rh-zero-divisor-geometry/positive-density-transverse-divisor-relocation-law.md`
- **Statement:** Any relocation of a functional-equation- and Schwarz-symmetric divisor from the
  critical line to a transverse position, preserving the ordinate counting measure exactly, must
  move zeros of **even** multiplicity. Consequently the blindness demonstrated by the relocation
  law is a statement about divisors with repeated on-line zeros, and says nothing about the
  simple-zero class.

## The elementary reason

Let `D` be a divisor in the `s`-plane invariant under the functional-equation involution
`s |-> 1-s` and under Schwarz conjugation `s |-> conj s`, and let

```text
mu(gamma) = total multiplicity of D at ordinate Im s = gamma.
```

Fix an ordinate `gamma != 0`.

* If every point of `D` at that ordinate lies **on** the critical line, the group orbit of a point
  `1/2 + i gamma` under the two involutions is `{1/2 + i gamma, 1/2 - i gamma}` — one point per
  ordinate. So an on-line zero of multiplicity `m` contributes `mu(gamma) = m`.
* If a point `1/2 + delta + i gamma` with `delta != 0` lies in `D`, its orbit is
  `{1/2 + delta + i gamma, 1/2 - delta + i gamma, 1/2 + delta - i gamma, 1/2 - delta - i gamma}`
  — **two** points at ordinate `gamma`. So an off-line zero of multiplicity `m` contributes
  `2m` to `mu(gamma)`.

Hence, at each ordinate, the contribution of the off-line part of a symmetric divisor is even.
If a relocation carries an entirely on-line divisor to one with an off-line part while preserving
`mu` pointwise, the multiplicity it moves at each affected ordinate must have been even. `∎`

## Verification against the existing construction

The relocation law's own example is exactly this mechanism, made visible by one identity. Its
envelopes are

```text
A_0(w) = cosh(w)^2,
A_a(w) = cosh(w-a) cosh(w+a),
```

and

```text
cosh(w-a) cosh(w+a) = (cosh 2w + cosh 2a)/2,
cosh(w)^2           = (cosh 2w + 1)/2,
```

so that

```text
A_a = A_0 + (cosh(2a) - 1)/2,        F_a = F_0 + ((cosh 2a - 1)/2) * C_beta.     (*)
```

`A_0` has a **double** zero at each `w = i pi (k + 1/2)`; `A_a` splits each of them into the
transverse simple pair `w = ±a + i pi (k + 1/2)`. Ordinates and total multiplicities agree at every
level, which is precisely why the ordinate counting measure is preserved. The construction is
therefore not merely compatible with even multiplicity — it *is* the splitting of a double on-line
zero, and by the theorem above it could not have been anything else.

Identity `(*)` also exhibits the whole relocation as the addition of a positive constant multiple
of the clean carrier `C_beta`, which is a sharper description than "two envelopes".

## What this changes

The relocation law is quoted (correctly, within its scope) as showing that the package

```text
{ functional equation, Schwarz symmetry, exact order one, hypertranscendence,
  ordinate counting measure, differential-translation field class mod DA }
```

is blind to on-line versus off-line placement. The theorem above shows the demonstrated blindness
lives on divisors with repeated on-line zeros. **Adjoining simplicity of the on-line divisor to
that package is not covered by the existing counterexample.**

This is a scope correction, not a refutation: the relocation law's conclusion stands exactly as
stated. What is removed is the tempting over-reading that no invariant in that package can ever
separate the two cases.

## Open question created

> **Q'.** Does a transverse relocation exist inside the class of functional-equation- and
> Schwarz-symmetric entire functions of exact order one with **simple** zeros, preserving the
> ordinate counting measure and the differential-translation field class?

Three honest remarks on `Q'` before anyone invests in it.

1. **It is not a route to RH by itself.** Simplicity of the zeros of `xi` is unproven, so a
   positive answer to "simplicity blocks relocation" cannot be applied to `xi` without first
   proving simple zeros — which is harder than RH is believed to be, not easier.
2. **It may well be answerable negatively and cheaply.** Relaxing "preserve `mu` pointwise" to
   "preserve the asymptotic counting function `N(T)`" restores enough freedom that a simple-zero
   relocation is plausible: one may trade multiplicities between distinct ordinates. Anyone
   attacking `Q'` should first settle which invariant is intended, because the theorem above is
   sharp only for the pointwise version.

# Continuous countermodel with an exact logarithmic counting remainder

- **ID:** CONTINUOUS-BEURLING-LOG-ERROR-AUDIT
- **Stage:** 3-formalized / not_new_scientific_knowledge
- **Type:** source-class audit and explicit auxiliary construction; not an RH architecture
- **Source:** `BeurlingRationalRealizability`, `BeurlingRegularIntegersOffLineZeros`,

- **Novelty:** not established; treat as an application of classical continuous Beurling constructions.

## Why this is needed

`regular_integers_do_not_constrain_zeros` chooses its model after the error exponent. Its Lean
statement proves positivity of a continuous logarithmic density and a rational transform identity,
not a counting asymptotic. Several descriptions reverse that quantifier order and infer universal
requirements on RH proof methods. Correct those descriptions independently of whether this repair
works. Continuous countermodels cannot eliminate a method whose additional discrete hypotheses
they do not satisfy.

## Concrete repair and paper proof

For real `g`, define

```
c = 4/27 + g^2/3,       r = 4/27 + 4g^2/3,
w_g(t) = (exp(t)+2-2 exp(2t/3) cos(g t)-exp(-t/3))/t,       t>0,
Z_g(s) = ((s-2/3)^2+g^2)(s+1/3)/((s-1)s^2),
J_g(t) = r exp(t) + (1-r) - r t - c t^2/2,                 t>=0,
j_g(t) = r(exp(t)-1)-c t.
```

The existing exponential factorization at `t/3` gives
`exp(t)+2-2 exp(2t/3)-exp(-t/3)>=0`. Adding
`2 exp(2t/3)(1-cos(g t))` proves `w_g>=0`. Its numerator vanishes at zero and is differentiable,
so the density is locally integrable at zero. Three Frullani terms, with pole parameters `1,0,0`
and zero parameters `2/3+i g,2/3-i g,-1/3`, give

```
exp(integral_(t>0) exp(-s t) w_g(t) dt) = Z_g(s),           Re(s)>1.
```

`J_g(0)=1`, `J_g'=j_g`, and `j_g(t)>=0` on `t>=0`: use `exp(t)-1>=t` and `r-c=g^2`.
Thus `J_g` counts a positive continuous measure with a unit atom at zero in logarithmic
coordinates. The elementary transforms of `1,t,exp(t)` yield

```
1 + integral_(t>0) exp(-s t) j_g(t) dt
  = 1 + r/(s-1) - r/s - c/s^2 = Z_g(s),                   Re(s)>1.
```

These identities explicitly pair the positive counting density with the positive logarithmic-prime
density at the level of their transforms. Lean proves the two integrability statements and transform
identities; it does not invoke a formal measure-uniqueness or convolution-exponential theorem. The exact counting formula is `N_g(x)=J_g(log x)` for `x>=1`, hence
`N_g(x)-r x = 1-r-r log x-c(log x)^2/2`. It has `O((log x)^2)` remainder and therefore, for this
**one fixed model**, `O(x^e)` for every `e>0`. When `g!=0`, `2/3+i g` is a genuine nonreal zero:
the denominator is nonzero there. The family is continuous; it is not a sequence of primes or of
unit-weight integers, and no functional equation is claimed.

## Exact formal result

`formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/BeurlingLogarithmicCounting.lean` contains 19 public theorems.
The premise-free `explicit_continuous_countermodel` instantiates `g=1` and packages:

- the counting primitive as `1 + integral_0^t j(u) du`;
- integrability and both transform identities for every `Re(s)>1`;
- the exact remainder `-13/27-(40/27)log x-(13/54)(log x)^2` for `x>=1`;

## The Logarithmic Counting Function of a Meromorphic Function

namespace ValueDistribution

variable
  {𝕜 : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [ProperSpace 𝕜]
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  {U : Set 𝕜} {f g : 𝕜 → E} {a : WithTop E} {a₀ : E}

variable (f a) in
/--
The logarithmic counting function of a meromorphic function.

If `f : 𝕜 → E` is meromorphic and `a : WithTop E` is any value, this is a logarithmically weighted
measure of the number of times the function `f` takes a given value `a` within the disk `∣z∣ ≤ r`,
taking multiplicities into account.  In the special case where `a = ⊤`, it counts the poles of `f`.
-/
noncomputable def logCounting : ℝ → ℝ := by
  by_cases h : a = ⊤
  · exact (divisor f univ)⁻.logCounting
  · exact (divisor (f · - a.untop₀) univ)⁺.logCounting

/--
Relation between `ValueDistribution.logCounting` and `locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting`.
-/
lemma _root_.locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting_divisor {f : ℂ → ℂ} :
    locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting (divisor f univ) = logCounting f 0 - logCounting f ⊤ := by
  simp [logCounting, ← locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting.map_sub]

/--
For finite values `a₀`, the logarithmic counting function `logCounting f a₀` is the logarithmic
counting function for the zeros of `f - a₀`.
-/
lemma logCounting_coe :
    logCounting f a₀ = (divisor (f · - a₀) univ)⁺.logCounting := by
  simp [logCounting]

/--
For finite values `a₀`, the logarithmic counting function `logCounting f a₀` equals the logarithmic
counting function for the zeros of `f - a₀`.
-/
lemma logCounting_coe_eq_logCounting_sub_const_zero :
    logCounting f a₀ = logCounting (f - fun _ ↦ a₀) 0 := by
  simp [logCounting]

/--
The logarithmic counting function `logCounting f 0` is the logarithmic counting function associated
with the zero-divisor of `f`.
-/
lemma logCounting_zero :
    logCounting f 0 = (divisor f univ)⁺.logCounting := by
  simp [logCounting]

/--
The logarithmic counting function `logCounting f ⊤` is the logarithmic counting function associated
with the pole-divisor of `f`.
-/
lemma logCounting_top :
    logCounting f ⊤ = (divisor f univ)⁻.logCounting := by
  simp [logCounting]

/--
Evaluation of the logarithmic counting function at zero yields zero.
-/
@[simp] lemma logCounting_eval_zero :
    logCounting f a 0 = 0 := by
  by_cases h : a = ⊤ <;> simp [logCounting, h]

/--
The logarithmic counting function associated with the divisor of `f` is the difference between
`logCounting f 0` and `logCounting f ⊤`.
-/
theorem log_counting_zero_sub_logCounting_top {f : 𝕜 → E} :
    (divisor f univ).logCounting = logCounting f 0 - logCounting f ⊤ := by
  rw [← posPart_sub_negPart (divisor f univ), logCounting_zero, logCounting_top, map_sub]

/--
The logarithmic counting function of a constant function is zero.
-/
@[simp] theorem logCounting_const {c : E} {e : WithTop E} :
    logCounting (fun _ ↦ c : 𝕜 → E) e = 0 := by
  simp [logCounting]

/--
The logarithmic counting function of the constant function zero is zero.
-/
@[simp] theorem logCounting_const_zero {e : WithTop E} :
    logCounting (0 : 𝕜 → E) e = 0 := logCounting_const

/--
The logarithmic counting function is even.
-/
theorem logCounting_even {f : 𝕜 → E} {e : WithTop E} :
    (logCounting f e).Even := by
  intro r
  by_cases h : e = ⊤ <;> simp [logCounting, h, locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting_even _ r]

/--
The logarithmic counting function is monotonous.
-/
theorem logCounting_monotoneOn {f : 𝕜 → E} {e : WithTop E} :
    MonotoneOn (logCounting f e) (Ioi 0) := by
  by_cases h : e = ⊤ <;>
    simpa [logCounting, h] using locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting_mono (by positivity)

/--
For `1 ≤ r`, the logarithmic counting function is non-negative.
-/
theorem logCounting_nonneg {r : ℝ} {f : 𝕜 → E} {e : WithTop E} (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    0 ≤ logCounting f e r := by
  by_cases h : e = ⊤
  · simp [logCounting, h, locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting_nonneg
      (negPart_nonneg (divisor f univ)) hr]
  · simp [logCounting, h, locallyFinsuppWithin.logCounting_nonneg
      (posPart_nonneg (divisor (f · - e.untop₀) univ)) hr]

/--
The logarithmic counting function is asymptotically non-negative.

# The Logarithmic Counting Function of Value Distribution Theory

For nontrivially normed fields `𝕜`, this file defines the logarithmic counting function of a
meromorphic function defined on `𝕜`.  Also known as the `Nevanlinna counting function`, this is one
of the three main functions used in Value Distribution Theory.

The logarithmic counting function of a meromorphic function `f` is a logarithmically weighted
measure of the number of times the function `f` takes a given value `a` within the disk `∣z∣ ≤ r`,
taking multiplicities into account.

See Section VI.1 of [Lang, *Introduction to Complex Hyperbolic Spaces*][MR886677] or Section 1.1 of
[Noguchi-Winkelmann, *Nevanlinna Theory in Several Complex Variables and Diophantine
Approximation*][MR3156076] for a detailed discussion.

## Implementation Notes

- This file defines the logarithmic counting function first for functions with locally finite
  support on `𝕜` and then specializes to the setting where the function with locally finite support
  is the pole or zero-divisor of a meromorphic function.

- Even though value distribution theory is best developed for meromorphic functions on the complex
  plane (and therefore placed in the complex analysis section of Mathlib), we introduce the
  logarithmic counting function for arbitrary normed fields.

/-!
## The Logarithmic Counting Function of a Function with Locally Finite Support
-/

/--
Definition of the logarithmic counting function, as a group morphism mapping functions `D` with
locally finite support to maps `ℝ → ℝ`.  Given `D`, the result map `logCounting D` takes `r : ℝ` to
a logarithmically weighted measure of values that `D` takes within the disk `∣z∣ ≤ r`.

Implementation Note: In case where `z = 0`, the term `log (r * ‖z‖⁻¹)` evaluates to zero, which is
typically different from `log r - log ‖z‖ = log r`. The summand `(D 0) * log r` compensates this,
producing cleaner formulas when the logarithmic counting function is used in the main theorems of
Value Distribution Theory.  We refer the reader to page 164 of [Lang: Introduction to Complex
Hyperbolic Spaces](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4757-1945-1) for more details, and
to the lemma `countingFunction_finsum_eq_finsum_add` in
`Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/JensenFormula.lean` for a formal statement.
-/
noncomputable def logCounting {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [ProperSpace E] :
    locallyFinsupp E ℤ →+ (ℝ → ℝ) where
  toFun D := fun r ↦ ∑ᶠ z, D.toClosedBall r z * log (r * ‖z‖⁻¹) + (D 0) * log r
  map_zero' := by aesop
  map_add' D₁ D₂ := by
    simp only [map_add, coe_add, Pi.add_apply, Int.cast_add]
    ext r
    have {A B C D : ℝ} : A + B + (C + D) = A + C + (B + D) := by ring
    rw [Pi.add_apply, this]
    congr 1
    · have h₁s : ((D₁.toClosedBall r).support ∪ (D₂.toClosedBall r).support).Finite := by
        apply Set.finite_union.2
        constructor
        <;> apply finiteSupport _ (isCompact_closedBall 0 |r|)
      repeat
        rw [finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset (s := h₁s.toFinset)]
        try simp_rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← add_mul]
      repeat
        intro x hx
        by_contra
        simp_all
    · ring

/--
Evaluation of the logarithmic counting function at zero yields zero.
-/
@[simp] lemma logCounting_eval_zero {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [ProperSpace E]
    (D : locallyFinsupp E ℤ) :
    logCounting D 0 = 0 := by
  simp [logCounting]

/--
Qualitative consequence of `logCounting_single_eq_log_sub_const`. The constant function `1 : ℝ → ℝ`
is little o of the logarithmic counting function attached to `single e`.
-/
lemma one_isLittleO_logCounting_single [DecidableEq E] [ProperSpace E] {e : E} :
    (1 : ℝ → ℝ) =o[atTop] logCounting (single e 1) := by
  have hΘ : (fun r ↦ log r - log ‖e‖) =Θ[atTop] log :=
    (IsEquivalent.sub_isLittleO IsEquivalent.refl isLittleO_const_log_atTop).isTheta
  have h₁ : (1 : ℝ → ℝ) =o[atTop] fun r ↦ log r - log ‖e‖ :=
    (hΘ.isLittleO_congr_right).2 isLittleO_const_log_atTop
  refine h₁.congr' EventuallyEq.rfl ?_
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop ‖e‖] with r hr
  simp [logCounting_single_eq_log_sub_const hr]

/--
A non-negative function with locally finite support is zero if and only if its logarithmic counting
functions is asymptotically bounded.
-/
lemma zero_iff_logCounting_bounded [ProperSpace E]
    {D : locallyFinsuppWithin (univ : Set E) ℤ} (h : 0 ≤ D) :
    D = 0 ↔ logCounting D =O[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) := by
  classical
  refine ⟨fun h₂ ↦ by simp [isBigO_of_le' (c := 0), h₂], ?_⟩
  contrapose
  intro h₁
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := exists_single_le_pos (lt_of_le_of_ne h (h₁ ·.symm))
  rw [isBigO_iff'']
  push Not
  intro a ha
  simp only [Pi.one_apply, norm_eq_abs, frequently_atTop, abs_one]
  intro b
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := eventually_atTop.1
    (isLittleO_iff.1 (one_isLittleO_logCounting_single (e := e)) ha)
  let ℓ := 1 + max ‖e‖ (max |b| |c|)
  have h₁ℓ : c ≤ ℓ := by grind
  have h₂ℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ := by simp [ℓ]
  use 1 + ℓ, (show b ≤ 1 + ℓ by grind)
  calc 1
    _ ≤ (a * |logCounting (single e 1) ℓ|) := by simpa [h₁ℓ] using hc ℓ
    _ ≤ (a * |logCounting D ℓ|) := by
      gcongr
      · apply logCounting_nonneg (single_pos.2 Int.one_pos).le h₂ℓ
      · apply logCounting_le he h₂ℓ
    _ < a * |logCounting D (1 + ℓ)| := by
      gcongr 2
      rw [abs_of_nonneg (logCounting_nonneg h h₂ℓ),
        abs_of_nonneg (logCounting_nonneg h (by grind))]
      apply logCounting_strictMono he <;> grind

/-!

# Descartes' Rule of Signs

We define the "sign changes" in the coefficients of a polynomial, and prove Descartes'
Rule of Signs: a real polynomial has at most as many positive roots as there are sign
changes. A sign change is when there is a positive coefficient followed by a negative
coefficient, or vice versa, with any number of zero coefficients in between.

## Main Definitions

- `Polynomial.signVariations`: The number of sign changes in a polynomial's coefficients,
  where `0` coefficients are ignored.

## Main theorem

- `Polynomial.roots_countP_pos_le_signVariations`. States that
  `P.roots.countP (0 < ·) ≤ P.signVariations`, so that positive roots are counted with multiplicity.
  It's currently proved for any `CommRing` with `IsStrictOrderedRing`. There is likely some correct
  statement in terms of a (noncommutative) `Ring`, but `Polynomial.roots` is only defined for
  commutative rings.

## Reference

[Wikipedia: Descartes' Rule of Signs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descartes%27_rule_of_signs)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Polynomial

section Semiring
variable {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [LinearOrder R] (P : Polynomial R)

/-- Counts the number of times that the coefficients in a polynomial change sign, with
the convention that 0 can count as either sign. -/
def signVariations : ℕ :=
  letI coeff_signs := (coeffList P).map SignType.sign
  letI nonzero_signs := coeff_signs.filter (· ≠ 0)
  (nonzero_signs.destutter (· ≠ ·)).length - 1

variable (R) in
@[simp]
theorem signVariations_zero : signVariations (0 : R[X]) = 0 := by
  simp [signVariations]

/-- Sign variations of a monomial are always zero. -/
@[simp]
theorem signVariations_monomial (d : ℕ) (c : R) : signVariations (monomial d c) = 0 := by
  by_cases hcz : c = 0
  · simp [hcz]
  · simp [hcz, signVariations, coeffList_eraseLead (mt (monomial_eq_zero_iff c d).mp hcz)]

/-- If the first two signs are the same, then `signVariations` is unchanged by `eraseLead` -/
theorem signVariations_eraseLead (h : SignType.sign P.leadingCoeff = SignType.sign P.nextCoeff) :
    signVariations P.eraseLead = signVariations P := by
  by_cases hpz : P = 0
  · simp_all
  · have h₂ : nextCoeff P ≠ 0 := by intro; simp_all
    obtain ⟨_, hl⟩ := coeffList_eq_cons_leadingCoeff (mt nextCoeff_eq_zero_of_eraseLead_eq_zero h₂)
    simp [signVariations, List.destutter, leadingCoeff_eraseLead_eq_nextCoeff h₂, hl, h, h₂,
      coeffList_eraseLead hpz]

/-- If we drop the leading coefficient, the sign changes drop by 0 or 1 depending on whether
the first two nonzero coefficients match. -/
theorem signVariations_eq_eraseLead_add_ite {P : Polynomial R} (h : P ≠ 0) :
    signVariations P = signVariations P.eraseLead + if SignType.sign P.leadingCoeff
      = -SignType.sign P.eraseLead.leadingCoeff then 1 else 0 := by
  by_cases hpz : P = 0
  · simp_all
  have hsl : SignType.sign (leadingCoeff P) ≠ 0 := by simp_all
  rw [signVariations, signVariations, coeffList_eraseLead hpz]
  rw [List.map_cons, List.map_append, List.map_replicate]
  rcases h_eL : P.eraseLead.coeffList with _ | ⟨c, cs⟩
  · simp [coeffList_eq_nil.mp h_eL, h]
  simp only [List.filter_append, List.filter_replicate, List.map_cons, List.filter, ne_eq, hsl]
  have h₁ : SignType.sign c ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra h₂
    suffices eraseLead P = 0 by grind [coeffList_zero]
    by_contra h
    have := coeffList_eq_cons_leadingCoeff h
    grind [leadingCoeff_eq_zero, sign_eq_zero_iff]
  simp only [decide_not, sign_zero, List.destutter, Bool.false_eq_true, reduceIte, h₁,
    decide_false, Bool.not_false, List.nil_append, List.destutter', decide_true, Bool.not_true]
  obtain rfl : c = leadingCoeff P.eraseLead := by
    have h_eL : eraseLead P ≠ 0 := by simp [← coeffList_eq_nil, h_eL]
    obtain ⟨ls, hls⟩ := coeffList_eq_cons_leadingCoeff h_eL
    grind
  by_cases h₄ : SignType.sign P.leadingCoeff = SignType.sign P.eraseLead.leadingCoeff
  · grind [SignType.neg_eq_self_iff]
  rw [if_pos h₄, if_pos ?_]
  · grind [Nat.sub_add_cancel, List.length_pos_of_ne_nil, List.destutter'_ne_nil]
  cases _ : SignType.sign P.leadingCoeff
  <;> cases _ : SignType.sign P.eraseLead.leadingCoeff
  <;> grind [= SignType.neg_eq_neg_one, SignType.zero_eq_zero, SignType.pos_eq_one,
      SignType.neg_eq_neg_one, neg_neg]

/-- We can only lose, not gain, sign changes if we drop the leading coefficient. -/
theorem signVariations_eraseLead_le : signVariations P.eraseLead ≤ signVariations P := by
  by_cases hpz : P = 0
  · simp [hpz]
  · grind [signVariations_eq_eraseLead_add_ite]

/-!
# Sign changes of a coefficient sequence, and peeling the lowest exponent

Two pieces of bookkeeping for the Laguerre induction on exponential sums.

* `signChanges` counts the sign alternations of a coefficient sequence, read in increasing order of
  exponent.  It satisfies the recursion that peels off the first coefficient.
* Once the exponents are shifted so that the lowest one is `0`, differentiating **removes** that
  term — its coefficient gets multiplied by the exponent `0` — and multiplies each surviving
  coefficient by a strictly positive number, hence leaves the sign pattern of the tail untouched.

Together: the derivative of a normalised exponential sum is an exponential sum with one fewer term
whose sign-change count is exactly that of the tail of the original coefficient sequence.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-! ## Sign changes -/

/-- Sign alternations of a list of reals: adjacent pairs of strictly opposite sign. -/
noncomputable def signChangesList : List ℝ → ℕ
  | [] => 0
  | [_] => 0
  | x :: y :: l => (if x * y < 0 then 1 else 0) + signChangesList (y :: l)

/-- Sign alternations of a coefficient sequence indexed by `Fin m`. -/
noncomputable def signChanges {m : ℕ} (c : Fin m → ℝ) : ℕ := signChangesList (List.ofFn c)

@[simp] theorem signChanges_zero (c : Fin 0 → ℝ) : signChanges c = 0 := by
  simp [signChanges, signChangesList]

@[simp] theorem signChanges_one (c : Fin 1 → ℝ) : signChanges c = 0 := by
  simp [signChanges, signChangesList]

/-- Peeling the first coefficient. -/
theorem signChanges_succ {m : ℕ} (c : Fin (m + 2) → ℝ) :
    signChanges c =
      (if c 0 * c 1 < 0 then 1 else 0) + signChanges (fun i : Fin (m + 1) => c i.succ) := by
  rw [signChanges, signChanges]
  simp only [List.ofFn_succ]
  rw [signChangesList]
  rfl

/-- Two reals of the same strict sign are simultaneously negative. -/
theorem neg_iff_neg_of_mul_pos {p q : ℝ} (h : 0 < p * q) : p < 0 ↔ q < 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro hp; nlinarith
  · intro hq; nlinarith

/-- Rescaling every coefficient by a factor of its own sign leaves the sign changes unchanged. -/
theorem signChangesList_congr_sign {l l' : List ℝ}
    (h : List.Forall₂ (fun x y => 0 < x * y) l l') :
    signChangesList l = signChangesList l' := by
  induction h with
  | nil => rfl
  | @cons x x' u u' hx hu ih =>
    cases hu with
    | nil => rfl
    | @cons y y' v v' hy hv =>
      have hprod : 0 < (x * y) * (x' * y') := by nlinarith [mul_pos hx hy]
      have hterm : (if x * y < 0 then 1 else 0) = (if x' * y' < 0 then 1 else 0) :=
        if_congr (neg_iff_neg_of_mul_pos hprod) rfl rfl
      rw [signChangesList, signChangesList, hterm]
      exact congrArg _ ih

theorem forall₂_ofFn_mul :
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (c d : Fin m → ℝ), (∀ i, c i ≠ 0) → (∀ i, 0 < d i) →
      List.Forall₂ (fun x y => 0 < x * y) (List.ofFn fun i => c i * d i) (List.ofFn c) := by
  intro m
  induction m with
  | zero => intro c d _ _; simp
  | succ n ih =>
    intro c d hc hd
    simp only [List.ofFn_succ]
    refine List.Forall₂.cons ?_
      (ih (fun i => c i.succ) (fun i => d i.succ) (fun i => hc _) (fun i => hd _))
    have hrw : c 0 * d 0 * c 0 = d 0 * (c 0 * c 0) := by ring
    rw [hrw]
    exact mul_pos (hd 0) (mul_self_pos.mpr (hc 0))

/-- **Positive rescaling preserves the sign pattern.** -/
theorem signChanges_mul_pos {m : ℕ} (c d : Fin m → ℝ) (hc : ∀ i, c i ≠ 0) (hd : ∀ i, 0 < d i) :
    signChanges (fun i => c i * d i) = signChanges c :=
  signChangesList_congr_sign (forall₂_ofFn_mul m c d hc hd)

/-! ## Peeling the lowest exponent -/

theorem expSum_succ {m : ℕ} (c a : Fin (m + 1) → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    expSum c a t =
      c 0 * Real.exp (a 0 * t) + expSum (fun i => c i.succ) (fun i => a i.succ) t := by
  rw [expSum, expSum, Fin.sum_univ_succ]

/-- With the lowest exponent normalised to `0`, differentiating deletes the lowest term. -/
theorem deriv_expSum_of_head_zero {m : ℕ} (c a : Fin (m + 1) → ℝ) (h : a 0 = 0) :
    deriv (expSum c a) =
      expSum (fun i : Fin m => c i.succ * a i.succ) (fun i : Fin m => a i.succ) := by
  rw [deriv_expSum]
  funext t
  rw [expSum_succ]
  simp [h]

/-- **The sign-change count of the derivative.**  After normalising the lowest exponent to `0`, the
derivative is an exponential sum with one fewer term, and its sign changes are exactly those of the
tail of the original coefficient sequence. -/
theorem signChanges_deriv_coeff {m : ℕ} (c a : Fin (m + 1) → ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ i, c i ≠ 0) (ha : ∀ i : Fin m, 0 < a i.succ) :
    signChanges (fun i : Fin m => c i.succ * a i.succ)
      = signChanges (fun i : Fin m => c i.succ) :=
  signChanges_mul_pos _ _ (fun i => hc _) ha

variable {R : Type*} [Ring R] [LinearOrder R] [IsOrderedRing R] (P : Polynomial R) {x : R}

/-- The number of sign changes does not change if we negate. -/
@[simp]
theorem signVariations_neg : signVariations (-P) = signVariations P := by
  rw [signVariations, signVariations, coeffList_neg]
  simp only [List.map_map, List.filter_map]
  have hsc : SignType.sign ∘ (fun (x : R) => -x) = (fun x => -x) ∘ SignType.sign := by
    grind [Left.sign_neg]
  have h_neg_destutter (l : List SignType) :
      (l.destutter (¬· = ·)).map (- ·) = (l.map (- ·)).destutter (¬· = ·) := by
    grind [List.map_destutter, neg_inj]
  rw [hsc, List.comp_map, ← h_neg_destutter, List.length_map]
  congr 5
  funext
  simp [SignType.sign]

end OrderedRing

section StrictOrderedRing

variable {R : Type*} [Ring R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] {P : Polynomial R} {η : R}

/-- The number of sign changes does not change if we multiply by any nonzero scalar. -/
@[simp]
theorem signVariations_C_mul (P : Polynomial R) (hx : η ≠ 0) :
    signVariations (C η * P) = signVariations P := by
  wlog! hx2 : 0 < η
  · simpa [lt_of_le_of_ne hx2, hx] using this (η := -η) (P := -P)
  rw [signVariations, signVariations]
  rw [coeffList_C_mul _ (lt_or_lt_iff_ne.mp (.inr hx2)), ← List.comp_map]
  congr 5
  funext
  simp [hx2, sign_mul]

/-- If P's coefficients start with signs `[+, -, ...]`, then multiplying by a binomial `X - η`
  commutes with `eraseLead` in the number of sign changes. This is because the product of
  `P` and `X - η` has the pattern `[+, -, ...]` as well, so then `P.eraseLead` starts with
  `[-,...]`, and multiplying by `X - η` gives `[-, ...]` too. -/
lemma signVariations_eraseLead_mul_X_sub_C (hη : 0 < η) (hP₀ : 0 < leadingCoeff P)
    (hc : P.nextCoeff < 0) :
    ((X - C η) * P).eraseLead.signVariations = ((X - C η) * P.eraseLead).signVariations := by
  obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_one.mpr (natDegree_pos_of_nextCoeff_ne_zero hc.ne)
  have hndxP : natDegree ((X - C η) * P) = P.natDegree + 1 := by
    have hPn0 : P ≠ 0 :=
      leadingCoeff_ne_zero.mp hP₀.ne'
    rw [natDegree_mul (X_sub_C_ne_zero η) hPn0, natDegree_X_sub_C, add_comm]
  have hndxeP : natDegree ((X - C η) * P.eraseLead) = P.natDegree := by
    have hePn0 : P.eraseLead ≠ 0 :=
      mt nextCoeff_eq_zero_of_eraseLead_eq_zero hc.ne
    rw [natDegree_mul (X_sub_C_ne_zero η) hePn0, natDegree_X_sub_C, add_comm]
    exact natDegree_eraseLead_add_one hc.ne

/-!
# Milnor symbols are permutation invariant up to sign

Interchanging two adjacent entries of a Milnor symbol negates its class, so permuting the entries
changes the class only by a sign.

* `milnorClassDeg_perm` : **a permutation of the entries changes the class by an integer factor.**
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- **Permuting the entries of a symbol changes its class by a sign.** -/
theorem milnorClassDeg_perm :
    ∀ {l l' : List Kˣ}, l.Perm l' → ∀ (pre : List Kˣ) {n : ℕ}
      (h : (pre ++ l).length = n) (h' : (pre ++ l').length = n),
      ∃ ε : ℤ, milnorClassDeg K n ⟨pre ++ l, h⟩ = ε • milnorClassDeg K n ⟨pre ++ l', h'⟩ := by
  intro l l' hperm
  induction hperm with
  | nil =>
      intro pre n h h'
      exact ⟨1, by rw [one_zsmul]⟩
  | cons x hp ih =>
      intro pre n h h'
      have hcast1 : ∀ (t : List Kˣ) (ht : (pre ++ x :: t).length = n),
          milnorClassDeg K n ⟨pre ++ x :: t, ht⟩
            = milnorClassDeg K n ⟨(pre ++ [x]) ++ t, by simpa using ht⟩ := by
        intro t ht
        exact congrArg (milnorClassDeg K n) (Subtype.ext (by simp))
      rw [hcast1 _ h, hcast1 _ h']
      exact ih (pre ++ [x]) _ _
  | swap x y t =>
      intro pre n h h'
      have hn : (pre ++ t).length + 2 = n := by
        simp only [List.length_append, List.length_cons] at h ⊢
        omega
      refine ⟨-1, ?_⟩
      show twoSlot pre t hn y x = (-1 : ℤ) • twoSlot pre t hn x y
      rw [twoSlot_swap, neg_one_zsmul]
  | @trans a b c hp₁ hp₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
      intro pre n h h'
      have hmid : (pre ++ b).length = n := by
        rw [← h]
        simp only [List.length_append]
        rw [hp₁.length_eq]
      obtain ⟨ε₁, hε₁⟩ := ih₁ pre h hmid
      obtain ⟨ε₂, hε₂⟩ := ih₂ pre hmid h'
      exact ⟨ε₁ * ε₂, by rw [hε₁, hε₂, mul_smul]⟩

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry
